answer: An operator running 176 keys as a result burns for 176 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the beacon salt is published after the vertex checkpoint, the ripple audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 160 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
